title: Meet comparing words with ==
idea: Just like numbers, two strings can be compared with ==. It is True only when the words match exactly. Meet it with visible output.

exercises.prompt: You already compare numbers with ==. The new idea is that == also works on...
exercises.explanation: == compares values of the same kind. For strings it asks: are these two words exactly the same?

exercises.prompt:
What is the value of this?

"cat" == "cat"
exercises.explanation: The two words are identical, so == gives True. String comparison asks for an exact match.

exercises.prompt:
What is the value of this?

"cat" == "dog"
exercises.explanation: Different words, so they are not equal - False. Only an exact match gives True.
color holds "red", and "red" == "red" is True, so the if branch prints "Stop".

exercises.prompt: Same code, but color = "green". What prints?
exercises.explanation: "green" == "red" is False, so the else runs: "Go".

exercises.prompt: A string variable can now hold a word, and you can test that word with ==.
exercises.explanation: Yes - strings are in scope, so a variable like color = "red" is fine, and color == "red" tests it.

exercises.prompt:
Fill the blank so it checks the word equals "yes":

answer = "yes"
if answer ____ "yes":
    print("Confirmed")
exercises.explanation: == tests equality for words too. answer == "yes" is True, so "Confirmed" prints.

exercises.prompt: Why must the word on the right be in quotes, as in color == "red"?
options: Quotes mark it as the text to compare against; without them Python looks for a variable named red
exercises.explanation: "red" is literal text. Dropping the quotes would make Python search for a variable called red - likely an error.

exercises.prompt: Match each comparison to its value.
exercises.explanation: Identical words give True; different words give False. Exact match is the whole rule.

options: It lets a program react to which word it was given, like "red" or "yes"
exercises.explanation: Deciding based on words - a command, a color, an answer - is how programs respond to choices made in text.
